definitions.explanation: An involuntary shaking of the body or a part of the body, caused by cold, fear, excitement, illness, or other strong physical or emotional states.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}さで{体|からだ}に{震|ふる}えが{来|き}た。
examples.english: My body started shivering from the cold.

examples.japanese: {恐怖|きょうふ}で{声|こえ}に{震|ふる}えが{混|ま}じっていた。
examples.english: There was a tremor in her voice from fear.

notes:
The noun form of the verb {震|ふる}える (to tremble/shake). Refers to involuntary shaking caused by cold, fear, excitement, illness, or other strong physical or emotional states.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {震|ふる}えが{止|と}まらない: can't stop shaking
- {震|ふる}えが{来|く}る: start trembling
- {声|こえ}の{震|ふる}え: tremor in the voice
- {手|て}の{震|ふる}え: hand tremor
- {体|からだ}の{震|ふる}え: body shaking

WRITING:
Can also be written as {振|ふる}え, though {震|ふる}え is more common for involuntary shaking. {振|ふる}え tends to be used for deliberate or mechanical vibrations.

RELATED WORDS:
- {震|ふる}える: to tremble, to shake (verb)
- {身震|みぶる}い: a shudder (often from cold or fear)
- {戦慄|せんりつ}: shudder of horror (literary)
